record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures on Rational Systems in Three Dimensions
record.original_question: For every special case of the three-dimensional rational system x_{n+1} = (alpha_1 + beta_1 x_n + gamma_1 y_n + delta_1 z_n)/(A_1 + B_1 x_n + C_1 y_n + D_1 z_n), y_{n+1} = (alpha_2 + beta_2 x_n + gamma_2 y_n + delta_2 z_n)/(A_2 + B_2 x_n + C_2 y_n + D_2 z_n), and z_{n+1} = (alpha_3 + beta_3 x_n + gamma_3 y_n + delta_3 z_n)/(A_3 + B_3 x_n + C_3 y_n + D_3 z_n), with nonnegative parameters, nonnegative initial conditions, positive denominators, and unbounded solutions, how do the solutions become unbounded, what are the stable and unstable manifolds of the equilibrium points, what invariants exist, and do periodic trichotomies occur?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the three-dimensional rational system of difference equations
  x_{n+1} = (α₁ + β₁ xₙ + γ₁ yₙ + δ₁ zₙ)/(A₁ + B₁ xₙ + C₁ yₙ + D₁ zₙ),
  y_{n+1} = (α₂ + β₂ xₙ + γ₂ yₙ + δ₂ zₙ)/(A₂ + B₂ xₙ + C₂ yₙ + D₂ zₙ),
  z_{n+1} = (α₃ + β₃ xₙ + γ₃ yₙ + δ₃ zₙ)/(A₃ + B₃ xₙ + C₃ yₙ + D₃ zₙ),
where all parameters α_i, β_i, γ_i, δ_i, A_i, B_i, C_i, D_i (i = 1, 2, 3) are nonnegative real numbers, the initial conditions (x₀, y₀, z₀) are nonnegative, and the parameters are chosen so that each denominator is strictly positive along every orbit. By a "special case" of the system one means a choice of which of the 24 parameters are zero and which are positive (after normalization), restricted to those special cases that admit unbounded solutions for some choice of admissible parameters and initial conditions.

For every such special case admitting unbounded solutions, determine:
(1) the precise mechanism by which solutions become unbounded (e.g., monotone divergence of a coordinate, oscillatory unboundedness, escape along specific invariant sets, etc.);
(2) the local stable and unstable manifolds of each equilibrium point of the system, including their dimensions and geometric description;
(3) all (rational or otherwise) invariants of the dynamics, i.e., functions I(x, y, z) that are constant along every orbit; and
(4) whether the system exhibits a periodic trichotomy, that is, a classification of the parameter space into three regions characterized by (i) global attraction to a unique equilibrium, (ii) every solution converging to a periodic cycle of some fixed period, and (iii) the existence of unbounded solutions, and if so, identify the precise trichotomy.
artifact.status_search_result: The questions concerning unboundedness mechanisms, stable/unstable manifolds, invariants, and periodic trichotomies for three-dimensional rational systems with linear/linear right-hand sides are part of a broad research program initiated by Camouzis, Ladas, and collaborators. While many lower-dimensional and special-case results exist (and seven periodic trichotomies are known in the third-order scalar setting), the general program for all special cases of the three-dimensional system remains largely open, and no comprehensive resolution has been published.

status_evidence.title: Dynamics of Third-Order Rational Difference Equations with Open Problems and Conjectures
status_evidence.snippet: Examines 135 special cases of rational difference equations, periodic trichotomies, and open problems on boundedness, stability, and convergence.
status_evidence.claim: Periodic trichotomies and unboundedness mechanisms remain a central open program in the theory of rational difference systems.

status_evidence.title: Input-output criteria for the trichotomic behaviors of discrete dynamical systems
status_evidence.snippet: Recent work on trichotomic behaviors of discrete dynamical systems.
status_evidence.claim: Trichotomy questions for discrete systems continue to be actively investigated.
